An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 31 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32 33 Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 36 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 37 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 38 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 39 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 40 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 41 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 42 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 43 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 44 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 45 46 Page 47 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 48 - The page loads the script with a `

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

# Decisions — owner: supervisor

- File layout: `server.mjs` (backend), `public/index.html` + `public/app.js` (frontend; server reads them and serves at `GET /` and `GET /app.js`, resolved relative to server.mjs via import.meta.url), `test/*.test.mjs` (testing), `package.json` (`"type": "module"`, `"start": "node server.mjs"`, `"test": "node --test test/"`), `README.md` (docs).
- Data file layout: `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [ {id, room, title, date, start, end}, ... ]}`. On load, validate strictly (object, integer nextId >= 1, bookings array of well-formed bookings with id < nextId); anything else → `cannot read data file <name>`.
- Save: write a temp file next to the data file then rename (atomic); a failed save rolls back memory. All mutations serialized through one in-process queue/lock.
- Strict readings: where a spec line reads two ways, build the stricter reading.
- 2026-11-02 · frontend · A success-status reply (200) whose JSON lacks the expected `rooms`/`bookings` array shows `Request failed.` in `#error` and changes nothing else (latest list fetch only). Why: spec is silent; avoids an uncaught TypeError and matches the "error message otherwise" fallback.
- 2026-11-02 · frontend · `node --test test/` (directory arg) fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on this Node 22.23; the package.json "test" script should be `node --test` (default discovery) or a glob. Why: verified by running it.

content.text:
The fix-round-1 code passes: overall 9/10, with no item under 8. I re-checked every line of the spec's Page section (lines 46-66, including the browser-API whitelist on line 50) against `public/index.html` and `public/app.js` and found no mismatches. All 52 tests pass when I ran them myself.

**Previous fixes, all done:**
- **Fetch options:** built as one object (`app.js:25-27`). POST sends only `method`, `headers` and `body`; DELETE and GET send only `method`.
- **Wrong-shape 200 replies:** these now show `Request failed.` and change nothing else (`app.js:63-67`, `107-111`). This matches the logged decision.
- **New tests, all present:**
  - latest list fetch that fails or gets no reply (`page-list.test.mjs:40-56`)
  - success leaves `#error` alone (`:58`)
  - earlier fetch succeeding after a later one is ignored (`:67`)
  - Book is enabled before the next step, on 201 and on 409 (`:83`, `:92`); the 409 test uses an `onTextSet` hook to prove the order
  - POST 201 with unreadable JSON (`:104`)
  - Cancel 404 re-enables the button (`:116`)

**Whitelist (spec line 50):** the test harness runs `app.js` in a `vm` context that only has `document` and `fetch`. So any browser API outside the list would fail at runtime, which is a strong check. `app.js` uses only listed members, and the only other globals are `JSON` and `Array`, which are plain JavaScript rather than browser APIs.

**Small problems left (none block the pass):**
1. `app.js:39` and `app.js:45` each write their own "is this an object" check, and they disagree: `listField` accepts arrays, `errorMessage` rejects them. One shared helper would fix both.
2. `app.js:112`: a reply whose `bookings` array holds `null` makes `bookingItem` throw. Because `loadList()` isn't awaited, that becomes an unhandled rejection. It only happens if the server misbehaves, so it's minor.
3. Duplicated test setup: `withList`, `APP` and `NO_REPLY` are written out in both `test/page.test.mjs` (lines 5-18) and `test/page-list.test.mjs` (lines 5-19). They belong in `test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs`.
4. Gaps where a plausible wrong version would still pass:
   - Every Cancel test uses a booking with `id: 1`, so code that used the list position + 1 instead of the booking's id would pass.
   - The filter test value `2026-11-03` doesn't change when URL-encoded, so it can't catch the value being altered. The only guard is a text search for `encodeURIComponent`.
   - No test sends a non-204 DELETE reply with unreadable JSON, which the spec says counts as no reply.

Coverage numbers don't include `app.js`, because it runs inside `vm`. From reading the tests, every branch in it is exercised.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — one IIFE with small single-purpose functions, shallow nesting, nodes built fresh; listGeneration is the only necessary mutable state
naming: 9 — clear, consistent names (request, errorMessage, listField, showOutcomeError, bookingItem)
duplication: 8 — the object-check is written twice with different array handling; withList/APP/NO_REPLY repeated across two test files
size: 10 — app.js 163 lines, all functions well under 50 lines, test files 79-232 lines
errors: 9 — explicit no-reply/error-status/wrong-shape paths, deliberate documented catch; a malformed booking entry would throw unhandled in loadList
tests: 9 — all requested tests added, the vm sandbox enforces the whitelist, ordering tests are strong; gaps on Cancel id, filter value encoding, and DELETE non-204 bad JSON
security: 10 — textContent/append only, no HTML injection, no absolute URLs or secrets
leftovers: 10 — no console, debug or commented-out code; comments are explanatory
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/public/app.js:39 extract one shared object check (rejecting arrays) and use it in both errorMessage and listField (line 45)
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/public/app.js:112 guard or catch a non-object booking entry so loadList cannot cause an unhandled rejection (e.g. treat it as the wrong-shape fallback)
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.test.mjs:5 move APP, NO_REPLY and withList (lines 5-18, duplicated at test/page-list.test.mjs:5-19) into test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.test.mjs:197 add a Cancel test with a booking id other than 1 (e.g. 7 as the second item) and assert the URL is /api/bookings/7
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page.test.mjs:86 add a filter value that changes when encoded (e.g. `a b&c`) and assert it reaches the URL unchanged
- /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/page-list.test.mjs:139 add a DELETE 404 with unreadable JSON test asserting the no-reply message and no list refetch
